student_learning_goal: I can sort shapes by sides, angles, and symmetry.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can sort shapes by sides, angles, and symmetry.
header.character_watermark: Symmy in the top-right with a small mirror. Small (~1.5in). References blueprint.recurring_characters.

parts.student_instructions: Look at each shape. Write number of sides and angles.

image_placeholders.description: 6 shapes in a 3x2 grid for a Grade 2 worksheet, B&W line art. Triangle, square, rectangle, hexagon, pentagon, octagon. Each ~1.5in. Below each: 'Sides: ___ Angles: ___'.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: WS01_P1_SHAPES at Part 1: keywords name the attributes.

parts.answer_key: Triangle: 3, 3. Square: 4, 4. Rectangle: 4, 4. Hexagon: 6, 6. Pentagon: 5, 5. Octagon: 8, 8.

parts.student_instructions: Draw lines of symmetry on each shape.
parts.visual_layout: Four shapes stacked vertically (square, equilateral triangle, rectangle, letter F) with generous space for drawing symmetry lines on each.

image_placeholders.description: 4 shapes stacked vertically for Grade 2 worksheet, B&W line art. Square, equilateral triangle, rectangle, letter F. Each ~2in. Generous space for drawing symmetry lines.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: WS01_P2_SYM at Part 2: keywords name the activity.

parts.answer_key: Square: 4 lines. Triangle: 3 lines. Rectangle: 2 lines. F: 0 lines.

parts.student_instructions: Sort 6 shapes by NUMBER OF SIDES.
parts.visual_layout: Sort table with 3 columns: 3 sides / 4 sides / 5+ sides.

image_placeholders.description: A 3-column sort table for Grade 2 worksheet. Columns: '3 sides' / '4 sides' / '5+ sides'. Below: 6 shape thumbnails to sort.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: WS01_P3_SORT at Part 3: keywords name the activity.

parts.answer_key: Distribute 6 shapes across 3 columns by side count.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, draw a shape with 5 lines of symmetry.
teacher_notes: Lesson 1 consolidation. Use Part 1 as diagnostic. Part 1 includes 1-2 transfer shapes (irregular pentagon, arrow) to verify side-counting + symmetry generalises beyond the canonical shapes from the lesson.
